title: rwb-payment payment matching (application slice): the consumed operation names and elements, the workflow and activity names, the payment code and the missed-payment key, the owner of the treatment record and the account of the legacy AC1, AC3, AC4 and AC5 are settled by no single source
source: Work Package B2-P8-001 story line (service rwb-payment, patterns DP01, DP03, DP04, DP05, DP06, DP07, DP09, DP10, DP11, DP13, DP15, DP19); Template and Rules v1 R3, R5.4, R5.5, R5.7 and R9; legacy RWB-E2-008 sections 3, 4, 7, 11, 12, 13 and 16; TSD P8 Payments and posting v2 T3.1, T3.2, T5.2 and Appendix T-A; FSD P8 Payments and posting v3 A2.1, A2.2 and A2.1.4; P8 context pack
description: One combined row for the application slice of RWB-E2-008. (1) Consumption: the legacy story calls six Java interfaces of P3 and P1 and reads two ACE views; no published document fixes the target operation names, paths, payloads or errors for the payments read, the next installment date, the batch status, the open case, the running plans, the installment write, the parameters, the lists and the package read, so the story carries the placeholder and a fake per declaration. (2) Workflow naming: JOB-07 is a Quartz and Spring Batch job in the sources and an event-started workflow under DP-10, and no source names the workflow or its activities; the story names them as a design choice. (3) Data: the legacy story keys the proceeds row on payment_code and adds a payment_missed_event_key table, while TSD P8 T3.1 carries account_payment_id and the standard columns and no such key table; the TSD field set is kept and the key is the platform idempotency row. (4) Ownership: the plan scopes the treatment record of RWB-E2-004 and the package of RWB-E2-042 as P3 contracts (RWB-P3-E2004-CON, RWB-P3-E2042-CON), while the treatment entity is published by S2 rwb-treatment and the package by P7 rwb-decision. (5) ACE read: the legacy story reads v_ace_payment, v_ace_account and v_ace_batch_status directly; DP-05 and ADR-010 send the same facts through rwb-source-data's contract or the service's own granted views. (6) Coverage: the Work Package assigns AC2, AC6, AC7, AC8 and AC9 to this slice, so AC1, AC3, AC4 and AC5 and their test cases TC-E2-008-01, -03, -04, -05 and -10 are owned by no story of the split.
evidence: RWB-E2-008 section 12 names RuleEvaluator.evaluate, RecoveryDataApi.paymentsLoaded, CaseWorkflowApi.openCaseForAccount, TreatmentApi.runningPlans, TreatmentApi.recordInstallmentPaid, RecoveryDataApi.nextInstallmentDate and BatchStatusQuery.forSource as Java interfaces, and offers PaymentsApi.proceedsForCase as a Java interface; section 13 names the table proceeds, the index ux_proceeds_payment_code on payment_code and a new table payment_missed_event_key; section 11 lists DF-FIN-001 to DF-FIN-009 and DF-TRT-032; TSD P8 v2 T3.1 carries account_payment_id and no payment_code column; TSD P8 v2 T3.2 fixes LOV-MATCH, LOV-MATCH-TYPE and LOV-PROCEEDS-SRC; FSD P8 v3 A1.2 keeps FEAT-PAY-03 and FEAT-PAY-04 for E4; the Work Package acs field lists AC2, AC6, AC7, AC8 and AC9.
owner_role: Solution architect, with the owners of rwb-source-data, rwb-case, rwb-treatment, rwb-decision and the payment service
proposed: Declare the nine consumed operations on the per-service bases with one hop and a 2 s timeout and take the element names from the owners at review; keep the TSD field set and hold the payment code and the per-due-date key in the platform idempotency row; name the workflow matchPayments and its four activities as the design baseline; and record in the RTM that AC1, AC3, AC4 and AC5 of the legacy key are carried by no story of this split.

title: rwb-payment payment matching (contract slice): the element names of the nine consumed operations, the extra event payload fields, the operation the architecture lists and the ownership map does not, and the schema baseline of proceeds are fixed by no single source
source: Work Package B2-P8-001 story line (work type CON, patterns all twelve); Template and Rules v1 R4, R5.5, R7.2 s12, R8.2 and R9; legacy RWB-E2-008 sections 12 and 13; TSD P8 Payments and posting v2 T3.0, T3.1, T3.2, T5.3 and Appendix T-A; FSD P8 Payments and posting v3 A2.1.4; P8 context pack ownership rows
description: One combined row for the contract slice. (1) The legacy story gives Java interfaces and two operation rows, so the request and response element names of the nine consumed operations are a review baseline and carry the placeholder where no published document fixes them. (2) The event payloads of the legacy story list treatmentId, dueDate and amountDue for PaymentMissed and proceedsId, caseId and amount for ProceedsMatched; no source fixes the envelope elements, the subject, the schema registry naming, the matched treatment of a match or the case id of a missed payment. (3) Architecture v5 lists GET /cases/{id}/payments among the IN operations of the service while the Ownership Map carries only GET /proceeds and POST /proceeds/{proceedsId}/match, so the extra operation is not published. (4) The schema baseline fixes the field set of TSD P8 T3.1 and the standard columns of T3.0, but no source fixes the physical business key of proceeds, the exact index set, the retention, the partition or retention values of the topic, or a grant on the three v_ace_* views. (5) The legacy migration name V2_008__payment_matching.sql is the monolith's and has no per-service counterpart. (6) Status is Draft (realignment v1) and the baseline is published without an approval.
evidence: RWB-E2-008 section 12 lists the six Java interfaces and the two operations, section 13 lists the migration V2_008__payment_matching.sql, the index ux_proceeds_payment_code and the table payment_missed_event_key; TSD P8 v2 Appendix T-A gives API-P8-001 and API-P8-002 with their request, response and errors; TSD P8 v2 T3.1 and T3.0 give the field set and the standard columns; TSD P8 v2 T5.3 gives the three events as published without payloads; the P8 context pack ownership rows give two operations, the table proceeds, the events EV-11, EV-12 and EV-25 and the jobs JOB-07 and JOB-08.
owner_role: Contract owner of rwb-payment, with the owners of rwb-source-data, rwb-case, rwb-treatment, rwb-decision and the event platform
proposed: Publish version v1 with the two operations, the three event schemas, the nine declarations, the schema baseline and the message map; mark every unsettled element with the placeholder and one review row; gate the tag on the contract tests and on the schema lint; and let a correction of an element name be a patch and a shape change a new version.

title: rwb-payment payment matching (deployment slice): the login and secret reference, the replica and threshold values, the partition and retention values, the build ID policy, the backfill limit and the runbook ownership are fixed by no source
source: Work Package B2-P8-001 story line (work type OPS, lane L-P8-D, owner DEVOPS); Template and Rules v1 R4, R5.5, R5.7 and R9; legacy RWB-E2-008 sections 4, 5, 10 and 13; TSD P8 Payments and posting v2 Appendix T-A and T-B; FSD P8 Payments and posting v3 A2.1.4.3; P8 context pack (schema, base, topic, queue, namespace)
description: One combined row for the deployment slice. (1) Identity: no source names the login secret reference, the connection pool size, the replica counts or the resource requests of rwb-payment, and DP-02 and R4 require one login and one queue per service. (2) Event platform values: no source fixes the partition count, the retention, the replica factor or the offset policy of rwb.payment.events.v1, its retry topic and its dead-letter topic, or the replay procedure of a dead-letter message. (3) Observability: no source fixes the five alert thresholds, the aggregation window of the four series, their dimensions or the run window after which a missing execution is an alert. (4) Runbook: no source names the five runbook entries, their owner roles or their review cycle. (5) Run controls: no source fixes the backfill limit per run, the reuse window of an idempotency key, the build ID format or the worker versioning policy of the release. (6) Approval: the story carries no approval and the first environment is non-production. (7) The legacy story fixes no deployment value and names no identity; it assumed a shared recovery login and a shared job monitor.
evidence: RWB-E2-008 section 13 names a feature flag rwb.payments.matching, a folder and a package, and no deployment value; section 10 names roles and a service identity without a login or a secret reference; section 14 gives the five message IDs without a routing; TSD P8 v2 Appendix T-B leaves DL06, DL11 and DL35 open, and DL11 is the non-functional target values; FSD P8 v3 A1.4 states only that the data products carry today's business date or show their date as stale; the P8 context pack fixes the schema rwb_payment, the base, the topic, the queue and the namespace and no deployment value.
owner_role: DevOps team, with the platform administrator, the observability owner, the event platform owner and the workflow kit owner
proposed: Ships one chart with an api and a worker deployment, a migration job, the topic and the two consumer groups, five alerts with their runbook links, four dashboard series, the flag, the backfill and the rollback; take every threshold, count and limit as a value of the environment; and review the five runbook entries with the on-call rota before promotion.
